To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the appearance of mast cells at different times in different tissues of the mouse may relate to the capacity of those tissues to restore mast cell‐dependent immunological and inflammatory responses in congenic mastocytosis‐free mice that received an infusion of bone marrow from normal donors.
the time course of mast cell appearance in tissues of normal mice and in mice with mast cell deficiency is tissue‐dependent.
mast cells appear in the skin of WBB6FJ+/+ mice at 18 weeks of life, but not in congenic WBB6FjW/Wv mast cell‐defective mice until 20 weeks after infusion of normal donor bone marrow cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the number, distribution, and function of mast cells in vivo.
the regulation of mast cell development in the mouse.
the development of mast cells and the role that they may have in immunological and inflammatory responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mast cells are not essential for normal development in the stomach, skin, extrapulmonary airways, or lung parenchymal tissues of mice.

the time course of the restoration of mast cell numbers in WBB6F mice following bone marrow infusion is not the same in all tissues, and this may have important implications for studies of mast cell function in these animals.

the tissue‐specific appearance of mast cells after bone marrow cell infusion in mast cell‐deficiency mice is a function of the time required for the development of the tissue‐specific mast cells and the time required for these cells to reach their maximum density in normal mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mast cell‐dependent responses are more readily assessed in W/Wv mice than in BM→W/BM→Wv mice, but that the latter model may be more appropriate for assessing the role of tissue‐resident mast cells.
mast cells are not only important in the initiation of inflammation but also in the regulation of inflammation, and this is a function that is tissue dependent.

the time courses of mast cell development in the various tissues of +/+ and BM→W/wv mice are different, but that the time courses for the development of mast cell density in a given tissue are similar in +/+ mice and in BM→W/wV mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capacity to induce a mast cell‐mediated response in a particular organ of W/Wv mice may depend on the local mast cell number and the extent of systemic mast cell activation.
it is important to know when the target cells for a given immunological or inflammatory challenge are present in a particular tissue, and when they are present, what is their functional capacity.

the capacity to reconstitute a mast cell‐mediated response in a particular organ of the latter mice depends on local mast cell density as well as whether the immunological stimulus activates mast cells in only the challenged tissue or systemically, with attendant widespread release into the circulation of proinflammatory mast cell mediators.
